question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose "No error".

These are your slippers on the ground, isn't they?
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary issue in the sentence is the incorrect usage of the question tag "**isn't they?**"
 
• The subject "**slippers**" is plural, hence the correct question tag should be "**aren't they?**"
 
• The correct phrase should be "**These are your slippers on the ground, aren't they?**" ensuring grammatical correctness and clarity.
 
• Thus, the error is located in **part 4** of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"These are your slippers on the ground, **aren't they?**"*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "No error"** – This would be the correct option if there were no mistakes in the sentence, but there is an error in part 4.
 
• **Option 2: "slippers on the"** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **Option 3: "These are your"** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **Option 4: "ground, isn't they?"** – **This part contains the error, as previously explained.**
